headline: Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO 11 days after resigning, with input from the White House, and NLW argues the episode marks a new kind of 'too big to fail' for AI and a shift in the balance between state and private power.

themes.title: Huang returns to Nvidia
themes.body: NLW recaps the scandal that pushed Huang out, including news of a second affair with an Nvidia executive, a suspected Chinese spy, Megaspeed and export controls. Nvidia's board said it had input from senior levels of the US government and saw no national security risk. Trump endorsed the decision on Truth Social, and NLW reports shares rose nearly 35 percent, adding about a trillion dollars in pre-market value.

themes.title: Too big to fail, AI edition
themes.body: NLW argues Nvidia's rescue is a new flavor of too big to fail, driven by capital and soft power rather than financial contagion, and calls Nvidia the unofficial central bank of AI. He cites Paul Kedrosky's view that the White House runs AI capex as a proxy stimulus program, and sees the state-versus-private power balance as a major realignment that reaches model labs such as Anthropic.

whyItMatters: When governments step in to protect the leadership of a critical AI supplier, technology leaders should treat vendor concentration and political exposure in their AI supply chain as strategic risks, not only commercial ones.
